passage: When Tarun came home to Bhojpur after his first year in Delhi, his cousin Mukesh's wedding was already under way. Tarun walked into the courtyard and gave everyone the quick city namaste he used in college, palms together, a small nod. His Badi Bua's smile went thin. His cousin Saurabh, who had never left the village, bent at once to touch her feet, then the feet of each elder along the line. Tarun's face grew hot. He had done this all through childhood; how had he forgotten? Before the pheras, he went back to Badi Bua and bent to touch her feet. She put her hand on his head and laughed. "The city boy remembers." Later, when the priest walked in, the whole courtyard stood up together, and Tarun rose with them, watching Saurabh's lead.
